keywords.text: A rare phosphorescent moss that glows pale blue in moonlight and dims when disturbed.

features.name: Ash Sentinel's Watch
features.description: You can sense ash spirits within 30 feet of you, even through walls.

items.name: Cinder Lantern
items.description: Sheds dim light out to 30 feet, fueled by a single glowing ember that never burns out.

spells.name: Ashwind Bolt
spells.meta: Evocation · 1 action · 60 feet · V, S · Instantaneous
spells.text: A mote of burning ash streaks to a point you choose within range and bursts, dealing 2d6 fire damage to each creature within 5 feet of that point.

races.name: Cindershade
races.description: Folk born of smoldering hearths, said to carry a spark of the first bonfire.

traits.name: Ember Sight
traits.description: You can see normally in dim light and smoke as if it were bright light, out to 30 feet.

classes.name: Example Adept
classes.description: A caster attuned to ash and ember, trained to read omens in the embers of a dying fire.

traits.name: Ashcraft
traits.description: You can cast Ashwind Bolt once without expending a spell slot. You regain this use after a long rest.

feats.name: Ember-Touched
feats.description: You gain resistance to fire damage, and you can produce a small, harmless flame in your palm as an action.

backgrounds.name: Ash Wanderer
backgrounds.description: You grew up travelling the cinder plains between smoldering hearth-towns.
backgrounds.equipment: A set of traveller's clothes, a walking stick, a cinder-streaked journal, and 5 gp.

subclasses.name: Path of the Smoldering Hearth
subclasses.description: Adepts who learn to channel the warmth of the hearth fire into protection for themselves and their allies.

traits.name: Hearthbound
traits.description: While within 30 feet of an open flame, you gain extra hit points equal to your Example Adept level.

tables.name: Ash Omens
rows: A gust of ash swirls at your feet.
Distant embers flare brighter for a moment.
A faint smell of woodsmoke follows you for an hour.
The nearest fire crackles once, loudly.
A fine layer of soft grey ash settles on your shoulders.
You feel unaccountably warm for a minute.
